'''Algorand''' is a [[proof-of-stake]] [[blockchain]] and [[cryptocurrency]].<ref name="sbac">{{cite conference | last1=Gilad|first1=Yossi|last2=Hemo|first2=Rotem|last3=Micali|first3=Silvio|last4=Vlachos|first4=Georgios|last5=Zeldovich|first5=Nickolai|title=SOSP '17: Proceedings of the 26th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles|url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3132747.3132757 | chapter=Algorand: Scaling Byzantine Agreements for Cryptocurrencies|doi=10.1145/3132747.3132757 | access-date=2024-10-26|hdl=1721.1/137789|hdl-access=free}}</ref> Algorand's native cryptocurrency is called ALGO.

== History ==
Algorand was founded in 2017 by [[Silvio Micali]], a computer scientist and professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT).<ref name="bbceae">{{Cite web|last=Zhao|first=Helen|date=2018-02-23|title=Bitcoin and blockchain consume an exorbitant amount of energy. These engineers are trying to change that|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/02/23/bitcoin-blockchain-consumes-a-lot-of-energy-engineers-changing-that.html|access-date=2021-04-03|website=CNBC|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-02-15|title=MIT professor debuts high-speed blockchain payments platform Algorand|url=https://venturebeat.com/2018/02/15/mit-professor-debuts-high-speed-blockchain-and-payments-platform-algorand/|access-date=2021-04-03|website=VentureBeat|language=en-US|archive-date=December 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211224100622/https://venturebeat.com/2018/02/15/mit-professor-debuts-high-speed-blockchain-and-payments-platform-algorand/|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

Algorand's test network was launched to the public in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Algo VC Fund Raises $200M to Fast-Track Its Own Cryptocurrency|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/boston/inno/stories/fundings/2019/08/27/algo-vc-fund-raises-200m-to-fast-track-its-own.html|access-date=2021-04-03|website=www.bizjournals.com}}</ref>

The main Algorand network was officially launched in June 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-10-23|title=Bahrain's Shariah Review Bureau Certifies Blockchain Firm Algorand As Shariah Compliant|url=https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2019/10/153198-bahrains-shariah-review-bureau-certifies-blockchain-firm-algorand-as-shariah-compliant/|access-date=2021-04-03|website=Crowdfund Insider|language=en-US}}</ref>

On March 17, 2026, the SEC and the [[Commodity Futures Trading Commission|CFTC]] jointly issued an interpretive release that identified ALGO as a digital [[commodity]].<ref>{{cite news |title=SEC, CFTC Move to Define Which Digital Assets are Securities |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-03-17/sec-cftc-move-to-define-which-digital-assets-are-securities |work=Bloomberg News |date=2026-03-17 |access-date=2026-04-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=SEC Clarifies the Application of Federal Securities Laws to Crypto Assets |url=https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-30-sec-clarifies-application-federal-securities-laws-crypto-assets |website=SEC.gov |date=2026-03-17 |access-date=2026-04-04}}</ref> Previously, the SEC had named ALGO as an unregistered security in several lawsuits against cryptocurrency exchanges.<ref>{{cite web | title=SEC complaint against Binance | website=SEC.gov | url=https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/complaints/2023/comp-pr2023-101.pdf | access-date=2024-10-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=SEC complaint against Kraken | website=SEC.gov | url=https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/complaints/2023/comp-pr2023-237.pdf | access-date=2024-10-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=SEC complaint against Bittrex | website=SEC.gov | url=https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/complaints/2023/comp-pr2023-78.pdf | access-date=2024-10-26}}</ref>

== Design ==
Algorand can only be forked intentionally through [[Fork (blockchain)#Soft fork|soft forks]] and [[Fork (blockchain)#Source code fork|source code forks]].<ref>{{cite book | last=Arslanian | first=Henri | title=The Book of Crypto | chapter=The Emergence of New Blockchains and Crypto-Assets | publisher=Springer International Publishing | publication-place=Cham | date=2022 | isbn=978-3-030-97950-8 | doi=10.1007/978-3-030-97951-5_4 | pages=99–119}}</ref>

=== Consensus algorithm ===
Algorand uses a [[Byzantine fault|Byzantine agreement]] protocol that leverages [[proof of stake]],<ref name="sdcp">{{Cite journal|last1=Xiao|first1=Y.|last2=Zhang|first2=N.|last3=Lou|first3=W.|last4=Hou|first4=Y. T.|date=28 January 2020|title=A Survey of Distributed Consensus Protocols for Blockchain Networks|journal=IEEE Communications Surveys and Tutorials|volume=22|issue=2|pages=1432–1465|doi=10.1109/COMST.2020.2969706|arxiv=1904.04098|s2cid=102352657|issn=1553-877X}}</ref><ref name="doi.org">{{Cite journal|last1=Wan|first1=Shaohua|last2=Li|first2=Meijun|last3=Liu|first3=Gaoyang|last4=Wang|first4=Chen|date=2020-11-01|title=Recent advances in consensus protocols for blockchain: a survey|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s11276-019-02195-0|journal=Wireless Networks|language=en|volume=26|issue=8|pages=5579–5593|doi=10.1007/s11276-019-02195-0|s2cid=213063001|issn=1572-8196|url-access=subscription}}</ref> which contributes to its energy efficiency.<ref name="bbceae" /><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Alzoubi | first1=Yehia Ibrahim | last2=Mishra | first2=Alok | title=Green blockchain – A move towards sustainability | journal=Journal of Cleaner Production | volume=430 | date=2023 | doi=10.1016/j.jclepro.2023.139541 | article-number=139541| bibcode=2023JCPro.43039541A | hdl=11250/3102853 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>

The Algorand Foundation funded an article which claims Algorand's overall protocol framework is sound under certain conditions.<ref>{{cite conference | last1=Blum | first1=Erica | last2=Leung | first2=Derek | last3=Loss | first3=Julian | last4=Katz | first4=Jonathan | last5=Rabin | first5=Tal | title=Proceedings of the 2023 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security | chapter=Analyzing the Real-World Security of the Algorand Blockchain | publisher=ACM | date=2023-11-15 | page= | isbn=979-8-4007-0050-7 | doi=10.1145/3576915.3623167 | pages=830–844| hdl=1721.1/153140 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>

===Cryptographic sortition===
The core principle of Algorand consensus is the cryptographic "self" sortition. The sortition procedure runs locally and privately, on each node of the network participating in the consensus protocol, without a centralized coordination.<ref name="sbac" /> The goal of the sortition algorithm is randomly selecting a subset of users participating in the consensus protocol (committees) ensuring two properties: the sortition's result can be easily verified once it is published, while it can not be determined ahead of time by malicious adversaries. The number of selected users in the sortition (committee size) is defined as a statistical expectation on the outcome of a pseudo-random process. The likelihood that a given user will be selected (in the committee) is influenced by the number of ALGO tokens held by that user (the stake).<ref name="sdcp" /><ref name="doi.org" />

===Consensus steps===
Algorand's consensus steps are: block proposal, proposals filtering (soft vote) and committing the block (certify vote).{{cn|date=March 2026}}

====Block proposal====
In the first step the cryptographic sortition selects a subset of users (proposal committee) which assemble and propose a block for the next round of the protocol. At the end of the step there will be a few block proposals (the protocol is tuned with a statistical expectation of 20 proposals) with different random priorities. After determining if a user is on the proposal committee, that user can build a proposed block and gossip it to the network for review/analysis during the second phase. The user includes the result of the VRF (h) and cryptographic proof (𝜋) in their block proposal to demonstrate committee membership.<ref name="sdcp" /><ref name="doi.org"/>

====Proposals filtering====
In the second step the nodes in the network wait for an adaptive period of time (𝜆), measured by nodes' local clocks, to be sure that the block proposals gossiped in the previous steps have been observed.{{cn|date=March 2026}}

A new cryptographic sortition selects a subset of users (soft vote committee) to vote and reach a Byzantine Agreement (called "BA*") on the proposal with highest priority. When users have determined that they are in this second-phase voting committee, they analyze the block proposals they have received (including verification of first-phase committee membership) and vote on the highest priority one.<ref name="sdcp" /><ref name="doi.org"/>

====Certify block (commit)====
Once a threshold of votes is reached in the previous proposals filtering step, the third and last step of the protocol begins. A new cryptographic sortition selects a subset of users (certify committee) to vote and reach a Byzantine Agreement on the content of the proposed block with respect to the state of the ledger (e.g. the block does not contain double spending, overspending or any other invalid state transition between accounts).{{cn|date=March 2026}}

If the certify committee achieves consensus on a new block, then the new block is disseminated across the network and appended to the ledger.<ref name="sdcp" /><ref name="doi.org" />

===Recovery===
The Algorand consensus protocol privileges consistency over availability ([[CAP theorem]]). If the network is unable to reach consensus over the next step (or block), within a certain time, the protocol enters in a recovery mode, suspending the block production to prevent forks (contrary to what would happen in blockchains based on the "longest-chain principle", such as [[Bitcoin]]). The Algorand team claims the recovery mode of the protocol ensures that the block production resumes eventually, with no need of reconciliations or reorganization, if a Byzantine Agreement is reached again.{{cn|date=March 2026}}

===Network===
An Algorand network is a [[distributed computing|distributed system]] of [[node (networking)|nodes]], each maintaining a local state based on validating the blockchain and the transactions therein. Nodes are spread geographically, communicating with each other over the Internet. The integrity and the consistency of the global network state and [[distributed ledger]] is maintained by the consensus protocol. Algorand nodes communicate through message [[gossip protocol|gossiping]] (broadcasting) either in [[peer-to-peer]] or via relay nodes (which facilitate efficient broadcasting with minimal message hops and low [[latency (engineering)|latency]]).{{cn|date=March 2026}}

== Usage ==

In 2019, Algorand became a partner of [[World Chess]].<ref>{{cite news | title=World Chess announces plans for 'hybrid IPO' | website=Financial Times | date=21 November 2019 | url=https://www.ft.com/content/46547c2e-0c3b-11ea-bb52-34c8d9dc6d84 | access-date=2024-10-20 | last1=Bradshaw | first1=Tim | last2=Murphy | first2=Hannah }}</ref>

In 2021, Italia Olivicola, Italy's largest olive and olive oil producers' organization, partnered with [[Euranet]] to implement blockchain technology based on Algorand to attempt to address [[Olive oil regulation and adulteration|olive oil adulteration]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Una blockchain avanzata per il settore olivicolo-oleario di ItaliaOlivicola | website=TeatroNaturale.It | url=https://www.teatronaturale.it/pensieri-e-parole/associazioni-di-idee/36835-una-blockchain-avanzata-per-il-settore-olivicolo-oleario-di-italiaolivicola.htm | language=it | access-date=2024-10-20}}</ref> [[SIAE]], the Italian Society of Authors and Publishers, also announced a project on copyright management using Algorand in the same year.<ref>{{cite web | last=Monaco | first=Daniele | title=Anche Siae sperimenta gli Nft | website=Wired Italia | date=2021-03-25 | url=https://www.wired.it/economia/finanza/2021/03/25/siae-nft-diritto-autore-blockchain/ | language=it | access-date=2024-10-20}}</ref>

In 2022, Algorand's blockchain was used by [[Robert Irwin (conservationist)|Robert Irwin]] and the [[Australia Zoo]] for a series of NFTs.<ref>{{cite web | title=Robert Irwin announces Australia Zoo's first ever collectible NFT series | website=7NEWS | date=2022-06-12 | url=https://7news.com.au/sunrise/on-the-show/robert-irwin-announces-australia-zoos-first-ever-collectable-nft-series-c-7142702 | access-date=2024-10-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Venz | first=Sophie | title=Australia Zoo uses carbon-negative blockchain technology to release NFT collection | website=SmartCompany | date=2022-08-16 | url=https://www.smartcompany.com.au/finance/cryptocurrency/australia-zoo-blockchain-nft-collection/ | access-date=2024-10-20}}</ref>

In January 2023, Fideiussioni Digitali, Italy's initiative to reduce fraud in bank and insurance guarantees, selected the Algorand blockchain for a project to address fraudulent [[bank guarantee]]s.<ref>{{cite web | last=Hall | first=Ian | title=Public blockchain confirmed for Italian bank guarantees project | website=Fintech news for government and public sector professionals | date=2023-01-04 | url=https://www.globalgovernmentfintech.com/public-blockchain-confirmed-for-italian-bank-guarantees-project/ | access-date=2024-10-20}}</ref> In February 2023, the Algorand Foundation urged users to withdraw funds from the [[cryptocurrency wallet]] MyAlgo, as it had been hacked for $9.6 million the week prior.<ref>{{cite news |title=Algorand Hack Drains $9.6M From Crypto Investor Wallets |url=https://www.pymnts.com/cryptocurrency/2023/algorand-hack-drains-9-6million-from-crypto-investor-wallets/ |access-date=24 March 2026 |work=PYMNTS.com |date=28 February 2023}}</ref>

In 2024, [[CNBC-TV18]] reported that Algorand's blockchain was being tested for use in a digital identification to help women in India access public health programs.<ref>{{cite web | title=AlgoBharat & SEWA Partner to Launch Digital Health Passport for Informal Sector Women | website=CNBC-TV18 | date=2024-03-06 | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1L42Kygf2z0 | access-date=2024-10-20}}</ref>

The Algorand blockchain had its first tokenized money market fund launch in June 2024.<ref>{{cite web | title=First tokenised money market fund launched on Algorand | website=ThePaypers | date=2024-06-27 | url=https://thepaypers.com/cryptocurrencies/first-tokenized-money-market-fund-launched-on-algorand--1268830 | access-date=2024-10-20}}{{dead link|date=March 2026}}</ref>
